articles.title: Polyethylene glenospheres in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty have greater long-term implant survivorship than metallic glenospheres: A New Zealand Joint Registry Study.
articles.authors: Bayley S, Boyle AB, Frampton C, Poon P, Dalgleish A, Gao R
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty in New Zealand
articles.sample_size: 8,601 procedures (3,437 with polyethylene glenosphere, 5,164 with metallic glenosphere)
articles.outcomes: Implant survival and revision rates, Oxford Shoulder Score at 6 months, 5 years and 10 years, revisions for deep infection and dislocation
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacements using a polyethylene glenosphere had lower revision rates (43% lower) compared to metallic glenospheres over long-term follow-up. Patient-reported shoulder function was similar between the two types, but polyethylene glenospheres showed fewer revisions due to infection or dislocation.

articles.title: The impact of lateralization and distalization shoulder angles-A systematic review of range of motion and clinical outcomes following reverse shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Phua SKA, Soong TK, Ladermann A, Ho SWL
articles.sample_size: 2303 subjects across 12 studies (mean age 71.7 years, 62.6% female)
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, clinical outcome scores, complications including acromial stress, scapular spine fractures, and deltoid stiffness
articles.take_home: The angle measurements used to describe reverse shoulder implant position do not reliably predict how well patients will move their shoulder or their clinical results after surgery, although they may relate to some complications. These measurements are simple to take but may not help surgeons predict individual patient outcomes.

articles.title: Outcomes for the anatomic hybrid glenoid total shoulder arthroplasty system, A 6-year median follow-up.
articles.authors: Jaipal C, Eyre-Brook A, Vun J, Espag M, Cresswell T, Clark D, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomic hybrid glenoid total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Implant survival, glenoid component loosening, Oxford Shoulder Score, Constant Shoulder Score, range of movement (flexion, abduction, external and internal rotation)
articles.take_home: The anatomic hybrid glenoid shoulder implant had a survival rate of 97.6% at 7 years, with only one implant needing revision surgery. Patients experienced significant improvements in shoulder function, pain and movement that were maintained over the follow-up period.

articles.title: Development and Validation of the Shoulder Arthroplasty Risk of Non-Home Discharge (SHORD) Score: A Risk Stratification Model for Non-Home Discharge Following Primary Total Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Phadke RA, Salman SG, Khawaja SR, Fiedler B, Rana A, Hussain ZB, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective prognostic model development and validation study
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 29,382 patients (derivation cohort two-thirds, validation cohort one-third)
articles.outcomes: Non-home discharge after total shoulder arthroplasty; SHORD Score discrimination, calibration, and classification compared with existing risk tools
articles.take_home: The SHORD Score is a preoperative tool using only admission-day information that can predict which patients are at risk of not going home after shoulder replacement surgery, ranging from 0.4% risk in the lowest-risk group to 20.3% in the highest-risk group. It performed better than existing risk assessment tools and may help with early discharge planning.

articles.title: Postoperative Complications Following Shoulder Stabilization for Primary Versus Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Dislocation: A National Database Study.
articles.authors: Chow AK, Sribhashyam S, Velichala SR, Smith MS, Cassidy BP, Vanderbeck J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort comparison using national database
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years or older undergoing surgical repair for primary or recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation
articles.sample_size: 2,302 patients per group after propensity score matching (primary ASD vs recurrent ASD)
articles.outcomes: Recurrent dislocation, shoulder instability, reoperation rates, shoulder stiffness, rotator cuff tears, shoulder impingement and shoulder pain at 3 and 6 months post-surgery
articles.take_home: Patients having surgery for recurrent shoulder dislocation had significantly higher rates of further instability problems after surgery compared to those having surgery for their first dislocation. Higher body mass index and seizure disorders were identified as risk factors linked to instability after surgery.

articles.title: Variation of the definition of "survival" in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Fox HM, Glenn ER, Padley JH, Lee B, White J, Srikumaran U, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with at least 10-year follow-up
articles.sample_size: 9 clinical studies (493 shoulders) and 3 arthroplasty registries
articles.outcomes: 10-year revision-free survival rates for entire construct and metal components only
articles.take_home: When using consistent definitions, approximately 83% of reverse shoulder replacements survived 10 years without any component needing revision, and 90% survived without revision of the metal parts. Different studies and registries used different definitions of 'survival', making it difficult to compare results, so standardised reporting is needed.

articles.title: Prevalence and Severity of Spin in Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Evaluating Treatment for Shoulder Instability.
articles.authors: Dhunna DP, Cook A, Nguyen KT, Wu KA, Mai E, Warburton C, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
articles.population: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating treatment for shoulder instability
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and types of reporting bias (spin) using the Yavchitz taxonomy; association between spin and methodological quality (AMSTAR 2 scores)
articles.take_home: Reporting bias was found in 68% of systematic reviews on shoulder instability, with misleading reporting and interpretation being most common, and these biased reviews had significantly lower methodological quality. This suggests that patients and clinicians should critically appraise evidence syntheses on shoulder instability, as biased reporting may lead to incorrect conclusions about treatment effectiveness and outcomes.

articles.title: Myocardial Infarction Within 6 Months before Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Strongly Associated with Postoperative Complications.
articles.authors: Parmar RP, Sahni VS, Holle AM, Amini MH, McKee M, Lederman E, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national insurance database
articles.population: Patients undergoing total shoulder arthroplasty with a history of myocardial infarction within 2 years before surgery, matched to controls without prior myocardial infarction
articles.outcomes: Postoperative myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, prosthetic joint infection, and 90-day mortality
articles.take_home: People who have had a heart attack within 6 months before shoulder replacement surgery have a much higher risk of complications after surgery, including another heart attack. Timing, type and location of the previous heart attack all affect the risk.

articles.title: Is Global Scapular Morphology, and Particularly Posterior Acromial Morphology, Symmetrical in a Healthy Cohort?
articles.authors: Werthel JD, Ogor J, Le Brigand J, Morvan Y, Gerber C
articles.population: Healthy adults without structural shoulder abnormality on CT scan
articles.sample_size: 304 patients (608 shoulders); 204 patients under 60 years, 100 patients aged 60 years or older
articles.outcomes: Bilateral symmetry of scapular morphology across 15 measurements; comparison between age groups
articles.take_home: Healthy shoulders are generally symmetrical in shape, though younger people showed small statistically significant differences between sides that were not present in older people. People with unusually shaped shoulder blades tend to have the same unusual shape on both sides rather than just one side, suggesting this is their natural body type rather than an injury-related change.

articles.title: Effects of different postoperative rehabilitation approaches following shoulder arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Zou J, Shi Y, Remis A, Liu S, Hao J
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, patient-reported outcomes, pain, forward flexion at 3 and 6 months, lesser tuberosity healing
articles.take_home: After reverse total shoulder arthroplasty, doing rehabilitation exercises at home works just as well as going to a physiotherapy clinic. Early mobilisation gives temporary benefits but makes little difference by 6 months, and there is no evidence that special subscapularis exercises provide extra benefit.
